subject: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks, owners, timelines
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks, owners, timelines

Hi Alicia — great to meet you on today's discovery call. As promised, I'm sending a concise draft for the MAP milestone focused on the Technical Evaluation so your team can confirm owners and timelines. I've attached a working spreadsheet (MAP_technical_milestone_v1.xlsx) and a short benchmark spec (benchmark_spec_v1.pdf).

Summary (proposed):
- Milestone name: Technical evaluation (proof-of-performance)
- Goal: Validate that Redwood meets HealthGrid's latency, cost, and functional quality requirements for the targeted production workload
- Success criteria (high level):
  • Latency: p95 inference latency < 120ms for 512-token requests (we'll propose stricter targets per model)
  • Cost: incremental inference cost <= $0.40 / 1k generated tokens for the evaluated config
  • Quality: pass >90% of acceptance prompts in your eval set (we'll import your prompt set into our eval harness)
- Model shortlist (initial): Redwood-Instruct-14B (quant), Llama-2-13B-chat (quant), Mistral-7B-instruct
- Test slate: 500 representative sessions (mix of short/long contexts), 20 guarded edge-case prompts for safety/consistency, throughput run for 1 hour at target concurrency
- Responsibilities:
  • HealthGrid: provide representative prompt set (CSV), sample production logs (anonymized), and a named owner for the evaluation (DevOps + App Owner)
  • Redwood (Karthik + Ben): run benchmarks on dedicated test harness, provide run artifacts (latency distributions, token-cost math, model outputs), and a short readout deck
  • Joint: agree on acceptance criteria and sign-off checklist in the MAP spreadsheet
- Timeline (proposed):
  • Confirm owners & datasets by 11/11/2026
  • Redwood runs benchmark 11/16–11/20
  • Readout and decision window 11/23–11/30
- Dependencies: sample dataset access, temporary test keys (we'll provide ephemeral credentials), and approval for model variants (quantized vs full-precision)

Ask: please confirm the HealthGrid owners (DevOps and App Product) and the target close date you want us to aim for (we've suggested 11/30 above). If possible, share a link to the prompt set (or upload to the Drive folder linked in the spreadsheet).

Thanks — copying Karthik and Ben to flag any immediate technical adjustments.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evan Kim <evan.kim@healthgrid.com>, Sasha Liu <sasha.liu@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks, owners, timelines

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We discussed internally and can commit to the proposed cadence with a couple of clarifications:

Owners (HealthGrid):
- DevOps owner: Evan Kim (cc'd) — will provide infra access and run any network/connectivity tests
- App owner / Product: Sasha Liu (cc'd) — will own the functional acceptance prompts and sign-off
- Security/Compliance contact: I'll coordinate through our GRC team if you need specific logs (TBD)

We can confirm owners and give you the prompt set by 11/11; I'll upload the anonymized CSV to the Drive link in your spreadsheet. The 11/16–11/20 benchmark window works. Two asks from our side:
1) Please include a short checklist for acceptable output fuzziness (how we label pass/fail for conversational answers) — Sasha can help define acceptable thresholds.
2) We prefer p95 latency target to be defined for both cold-start (first token after model load) and steady-state; if you can provide both numbers in the run artifacts that will be ideal.

Target close date: 11/30/2026 looks good for our internal calendar.

Alicia Torres
Head of Partnerships
HealthGrid
alicia.torres@healthgrid.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Evan Kim <evan.kim@healthgrid.com>, Sasha Liu <sasha.liu@healthgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmarks, owners, timelines

Thanks Vanessa / Alicia — quick technical slate from our side and one proposed measurement plan so we can align on exact pass/fail gates.

Proposed benchmark slate (detailed):
- Dataset: 500 sessions, ~4k unique prompts, mixed token lengths (50–1,500) — HealthGrid to provide CSV by 11/11
- Model shortlist to test (config + rationale):
  1) Redwood-Instruct-14B (INT8 quant candidate) — best balance of quality/cost for customer prompts
  2) Llama-2-13B-chat (INT4 quant) — good baseline open model for comparison
  3) Mistral-7B-Instruct — lowest-cost option, useful for throughput scenarios
- Metrics we will produce per model: p50/p90/p95 latency for 64/256/512 tokens, throughput at 8/16 concurrent streams, tokens-per-second, aggregate token-cost estimate using your traffic profile
- Acceptance gates (proposed):
  • Functional accuracy: >= 90% pass rate on curated acceptance prompts (Sasha to supply pass/fail rubric)
  • Latency: p95 <= 120ms steady-state for 512-token requests; cold-start p95 <= 300ms (we'll provide both)
  • Cost: projected incremental cost <= $0.40 / 1k output tokens for the chosen model/config

Measurement plan & responsibilities:
- Redwood (Karthik/Ben): deploy transient benchmark harness in our Dedicated test environment, run head-to-head model runs, collect artifacts, and produce a 6–8 slide readout deck. We'll also include raw latency histograms and per-prompt model outputs for audit.
- HealthGrid (Alicia/Evan/Sasha): provide prompt CSV, representative request distribution (tokens per request by percentile), and confirm any safety/guardrails to apply during test runs. Evan, if you can confirm how accessible a small test VPC or short-lived test key is, that will speed things up.
- Joint: sign-off checklist captured in the MAP spreadsheet columns (owner, target, actual, notes)

Suggested timeline (confirming Vanessa's dates):
- 11/11: HealthGrid uploads dataset and confirms owners
- 11/16–11/20: Redwood runs benchmarks (we'll reserve slots for the 16th and 17th for baseline runs)
- 11/23: Internal readout + Q&A
- 11/30: MAP sign-off and decision window

I'll add the measurement columns to the MAP spreadsheet and create a short runbook for the benchmark steps. If we need to shift the cost gate or latency target, flag it here and we'll update the spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick confirmations. Next steps from Redwood:
1) I will publish MAP_technical_milestone_v1.xlsx to the shared Drive folder and set editing to the listed owners (HealthGrid owners + Karthik/Ben).
2) Karthik will add the measurement columns and the runbook by EOD 11/10 (he's already on it).
3) Alicia/Evan/Sasha: please upload the prompt CSV and traffic profile to the Drive by 11/11 so we can lock the benchmark window.

I'll also send a calendar invite for a 30-minute readout on 11/23 (placeholder). If any of the proposed acceptance gates are blockers, let me know and we'll escalate to adjust the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this across the finish line.

Best,
